title: Goose v2 Necks QA
eyebrow: Ready for your check · Models #25, the goose v2 necks, with #18's fused skin · built on claude/project-thread-09ugci, not pushed

unverified: Nothing bends yet: the necks only look jointed. The 15 bones in the main neck and 12 in each side neck are built in #21 (the rig), and only a pose test there will prove the necks can move
Under the dark neck colour, the vertebra ridges read faintly; the bone spikes carry most of the segmentation, and they show best from behind
The colour is still the stand-in carried over from version 1, with a hard, ragged black-to-pale line across the breast. #20 (textures) will replace this colour
Nobody has opened goose_v2.glb or goose_v2.fbx in a game engine; the only thing that has run is the export from Blender
The model is 297,820 triangles, so #19 (muscle and feathers) has only 2,180 triangles left of the 300,000 budget and will have to save triangles elsewhere

short.lead: The necks are rebuilt as you approved. Each one rests in a goose's S-curve. The main neck has 15 vertebra ridges and each side neck has 12, with a bone spike tearing out of every vertebra along the back. The heads have not moved. The build passed all its checks: 297,820 triangles against the 300,000 budget, 6.750 m tall, and a skin that is still one piece. Version 1 is unchanged.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what was checked and what it needs from you.
items: A spike and a ridge at every vertebra
Seen from behind, the row of spikes and the bumps between them show each neck as a chain of vertebrae, from the root up to the head.

items.alt: The three necks from behind, each with a row of bone spikes and ridges
items.caption: From behind: one spike per vertebra.

items: Each neck leans forward low, bends back in the middle and tips forward to the head. The spikes along the back follow the curve.

items.alt: A side neck from the side, curving in an S with spikes along its back
items.caption: From the side.

items: Look at the necks and the review sheet

The sheet docs/art/reviews/goose-v2-review.png shows the concept, the four views and the join close-ups. Say whether the necks now read as jointed and flexible. If the ridges should show more strongly, that is one number per ridge in spec.json, and I can raise it.
